ORIGINAL ARTICLE
Multi‑objective approach for protection of microgrids using surrogate 
assisted particle swarm optimization (SAPSO)
R. Hannah Lalitha1 · G. Emily Manoranjitham2 · D. Weslin3 · A. Senthilselvi4
Received: 10 June 2021 / Accepted: 18 August 2021 / Published online: 6 September 2021 
© King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology 2021
Abstract
Despite of several formulations discussed for operation of Directional Over current Relays (DOCRs) in micro grids the coordi-
nation of DOCR is yet a great tasked to be solved. A micro grid is a group of generators preferably a renewable energy source 
and loads interconnected. The modes of micro grid operation, grid connected mode and autonomous mode are to be considered 
simultaneously to design an optimal protection scheme for the micro grid. Several conflicting objective functions that must be 
optimized simultaneously during the relay setting process make the coordination problem to be treated as multi-objective. In 
this work a multi-objective approach yielding better coordination is presented. There are two major objectives as follows; former 
is the synchronization period between the main and secondary relays, later is the relay operation time. The conventional Multi-
Objective Evolutionary Algorithms (MOEAs) may take thousands of function evaluations, which is not practical for real-world 
problems. Hence surrogates are introduced in those MOEAs to approximate the fitness function. The relay coordination is devised 
as a constrained multi-objective problem. The Surrogate Assisted Particle Swarm Optimization (SAPSO) Algorithm is applied 
to accomplish better coordination between the relays. The scheme is validated using standard IEEE systems and the results are 
compared with the conventional Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO). The optimal values of pickup cur-
rent and Time Dial Settings are computed for both modes of micro grid operation. The sum of operating time of all relays and 
the synchronization period between the main and secondary relays are minimized. The Inverted Generation Distance (IGD) is 
employed as the parameter for computing the performance of the algorithm. Also the convergence characteristic is analyzed. From 
the results it is proved that SAPSO have good stability than MOPSO and offers better Pareto fronts, convergence and distribution.
Keywords Micro grids · Relay coordination · Operating time · CTI and surrogates
Introduction
The need for electric power is growing rapid in the current 
scenario. The conventional energy sources known as non 
renewable source takes millions of years for their formation. 
The availability of these resources is depreciated. To over -
come these, new techniques for the production of electricity 
is proposed to meet the demand of the electricity with the 
advancement in the world. The concept of Micro grid is a 
solution to generate and distribute power which eliminates

the conventional resources for power generation. A micro 
grid is a group of generators preferably a renewable energy 
source and loads interconnected, that can be operated in con-
nection with the grid or operated autonomously ensuring reli-
able supply to the customer. For reliable operation, i.e., to 
minimize transmission losses and network congestion, these 
micro grids should be connected near the load. The micro 
grid consists of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and 
energy storage devices. The advantages of micro grids are 
energy efficient, reliable, economic, eco-friendly and reduced 
energy consumption. Under normal condition the micro grids 
are connected to the distribution network. Under abnormali-
ties it can be separated from the grid by static switch at the 
Point of Common Coupling (PCC) and operate autonomously.
Even so, there are many technical issues during the inte-
gration and operation of micro grids (Najy Waleed et al. 
2013; Haron et al. 2012; Sharaf et al. 2016; Bayindir et al. 
2014; Olivares et al. 2014). The voltage and frequency of 
the system is affected by the intermittent nature of DG. The 
variation in the load results in un-modeled dynamics. This 
un-modeled dynamics has impacts on the performance of the 
micro grid. The security, autonomous operation, recovery 
from planned and unplanned shut downs, relay coordination, 
reliability and disturbance in quality of power, cost recurred 
for the modern technologies are the vital issues need to be 
addressed in the micro grids.
One among the challenges in the integration of micro 
grid is the protection system. Distribution systems need to 
be protected from all the possible faults. When a fault occur 
only the portion of the system affected by the fault should 
be tripped, while the other healthy areas should be left 
unaffected. Protection coordination is designing protection 
scheme such that each relay operates as rapid as possible, 
but if the relay fails, the backup relay comes into action. In 
Conventional distribution systems, the power flow is unidi-
rectional hence the protection system is simple and so over 
current relays and fuses are installed to protect the system 
(Elmore 2003; Singh and Panigrahi 2014; Zeineldin et al. 
2006; Asadi and Kouhsari 2009). Due to the new concept 
of introducing generation in the distribution side (DER), the 
power flow is no longer unidirectional but becomes bidi-
rectional. This makes the protection scheme and hence the 
coordination of relays becomes complex.
Also introduction of DER affects the magnitude and direc-
tion of fault current. Hence the relays cannot perform their 
function correctly and there is a chance of miss-coordination 
between the relays. The fault current magnitude depends on 
the type of DG. For inverter-based DG, the fault current value 
is approximately. 1 p.u. The synchronous based DG has more 
values. The introduction of DER into the system makes the 
system more inter connected. Therefore the DOCR are imple-
mented to solve the coordination problem (Chen et al. 2013; 
El-Khattam and Sidhu 2008; Sortomme et al. 2009; Javadian 
and Haghifam 2008; Kamal et al. 2014). The abnormalities 
such as line outage, generator outage and substation faults, 
etc., may lead to miss-coordination of DOCR because vari-
ation in fault current cases. During failure of the supply, the 
micro grid is changed from grid connected to the autonomous 
mode and the network topology changes. The DOCR sense 
the current and voltage of the system and trip the relay if the 
fault is detected. DOCR determines the fault by considering 
the phase or of voltage and current. The relay finds the loca-
tion of fault. If the fault is located in front of the relay, then it 
will operate, otherwise it does not operate. The relay operates 
by comparing current in the circuit with the reference current. 
When the actual current exceeds the reference current; it is 
called short circuit current. This is used to identify the loca-
tion of fault. The magnitude of the fault current is inversely 
proportional to the fault location. If the fault is located far 
away from the source, the fault impedance will be high and 
therefore the fault current is small.
In protection system, the relays are considered as primary 
and backup relays. The relay responding fast to the faults is 
termed as primary or main relay. The relay operating after 
a short time interval when the primary relay fails is consid-
ered as backup relay. Since the main relay has number of 
backup relays for protection, the constraints imposed are 
relatively high. In event of this, the relay coordination in 
meshed power system is a great challenge for the researchers 
(Mohammadi et al. 2010).
The DOCR coordination issue is typically solved as a 
single objective optimization problem considering only one 
objective function. In general, the over current relay setting 
is proposed as several contrariant functions to be refined 
simultaneously. The coordination of DOCR coordination 
should conform constraints imposed by manufacturers such 
as the electrical and mechanical damage limits. Also the 
operation characteristics of the equipments such as the trans-
former in rush current, motor locked rotor current should be 
fulfilled. The incorporation of renewable sources as genera-
tors makes the DOCR coordination problem intricate com-
pared with radial power system due to the following reasons: 
the current direction and the short circuit components. The 
relay operating time is minimized by choosing optimal relay 
design variables such as pickup (PU) and time Multiplier 
Setting (TMS) settings of relay. The problem is formulated 
as multi-objective optimization problem as a new objective 
function which is the minimization of CTI, is added to the 
primary relay operating time function.
The advantage of the multi-objective optimization is 
simultaneous optimization of the two conflicting objectives 
(Benabid 2016; Díaz-Manríquez et al. 2016; Lalitha and 
Xavier 2019; Hussain et al. 2001; Liu and Yang 2012). Con-
ventional optimization techniques such as Newton method, 
steepest descent are used to solve many engineering optimi-
zation problems. But they have the limitations, that they are

not able to find a global solution in case of problems with 
multiple local minima. Hence the conventional optimization 
algorithms are replaced by global optimization algorithms.
The global optimization algorithms may be heuristic and 
meta-heuristic in nature. These algorithms are easy to imple-
ment and also efficient in nature. The types of nature inspired 
algorithms are GA, PSO, and Bacterial for aging algorithm, 
Cuckoo search algorithm, Firefly algorithm, Cat swarm opti-
mization etc. These algorithms are not knowledge based and 
provide better accurate results (Yang and Liu 2013; Mansour 
et al. 2007; Nigim and Lee 2007 ; Faisal Badal et al. 2019; 
Singh and Gupta 2012; Barzegari et al. 2010; Zellagui et al. 
2014; Yu et al. 2018). Even though these optimization algo-
rithms are useful to solve complex optimization algorithms, 
they are incapable when the objective function is computa -
tionally complex and expensive, since it requires high number 
of iterations and function evaluations. The time taken to com-
plete first iteration is somewhat high in these types of nature 
inspired evolutionary algorithms and it is not applied to real-
world optimization problems with large number of function 
evaluations. Hence nowadays, surrogate assisted optimization 
algorithms are used to solve the computationally expensive 
real-world optimization problems. These surrogate model are 
classified as Radial basis function (RBF), Neural networks, 
Kriging, etc. These reduce the complexity by approximating 
the function and thereby reducing the number of function 
evaluations and computational cost. These surrogate mod -
els will assist the evolutionary optimization algorithms to 
converge quickly. In this work, Surrogate Assisted Particle 
Swarm Optimization (SAPSO) is proposed for solving the 
multi-objective optimization problem in DOCR relay coordi-
nation (Korde and Bedekar., 2016; Amali and Baskar 2015a; 
Buche et al. 2005). The problem considered is multi-objective, 
since the objective function needs to be minimized comprises 
of both relay operating time and coordinating time (Lv et al. 
2019; Ratle 2001; Cai et al. 2019; Korde and Bedekar. 2016; 
Amali and Baskar 2015; Buche et al. 2005). The results are 
obtained for both grid connected configuration and double 
configuration. The simulation is performed by inducing faults 
in the middle of lines. Each relay operates for close end and 
far ends faults. In Grid connected micro grid configuration the 
system is connected to grid and the analysis is performed. The 
system is supplied from the grid and also from all the DG. The 
system is said to be islanded when there is no supply from the 
grid and is powered only by DGs.
Related work
The integration of micro grids its challenges and the control 
methods for micro grid operation have been proposed in 
Faisal et al. (2019). The voltage and frequency of the system 
is affected by the intermittent nature of DG. The voltage 
of the micro grid is regulated with the implementation of 
integral controller, PID controller and damping controllers. 
Also the variations in the load may result in un-conditioned 
dynamics. This dynamics effect the microgrid operation. The 
Micro grid is controlled by a central controller to estimate 
the amount of electric power supplied by the DG units. A 
decentralized control approach in which each unit has a local 
controller is also discussed. With these controllers desirable 
performance of micro grid is obtained. The opportunities 
and challenges faced while the integration of micro grid with 
existing utilities are discussed in Nigim et al. (2007). The 
coordination of DOCR coordination should conform con-
straints imposed by manufacturers such as the electrical and 
mechanical damage limits. Also the operation characteristics 
of the equipments such as the transformer in rush current, 
motor-locked rotor current are discussed. The incorporation 
of renewable sources as generators makes the DOCR coordi-
nation problem intricate compared with radial power system 
due to the following reasons: the current direction and the 
short circuit components The electric power pricing, incen-
tives to effective utilization of power, decision priority, risk 
responsibility and insurance for new technologies adapta-
tion, interconnection standards and regulatory control are 
analyzed. The reliance of import of fuel sources, efficient use 
of RES, electric power supplies to rural region, extension of 
transmission lines and career growth in modern technology 
areas are also presented.
Numerous literatures have been proposed for relay coor-
dination problem. Over current protection issues in a micro 
grid have been presented Waleed et al. (2013). The solutions 
include use of Fault Current Limiters (FCL), directional pro-
tection and designing the relays with two settings, one for 
grid operated mode and another for autonomous mode. The 
relay settings are computed considering the both modes of 
micro grids. The solution for the problem is obtained using 
constrained non linear programming and the optimization 
is carried out using Genetic Algorithm. The protection 
scheme can be implemented to meshed distribution sys-
tem with conventional synchronous generator. The FCL is 
connected in series with the main grid and along with the 
DOCR, to offer an efficient protection system. Over current 
protection relay operates when the load current exceeds the 
limit. The Tap Setting (TS) is the term referred as the current 
setting multipliers in over current relays which is normally 
50–200% increase Korde and Bedekar (2016). The maxi-
mum load current and minimum fault current can be used 
for measuring the TS Mohammadi et al. (2010). If a fault 
occurs in the system the relay should operate fast to clear 
the fault. If the relay fails, the backup relay should come into 
action after a time interval called Coordination Time Inter -
val (CTI) Eklas Hossain et al. (2014). The relay settings are 
mainly influenced by initial guess of the relay parameters. 
The relay coordination may depend on time grading, current

grading or both time and current grading (So et al. 1997). 
The optimum PSM and TMS and minimum operation time 
of primary relay are computed. Fault Current Limiters are 
implemented to reduce the DG fault current in El Khattam 
and Sidhu (2008). The relay coordination is restored without 
varying the relay settings. Also the analysis is carried out 
without disconnecting the DG at the time of fault.
The steps to select the resistive or inductive FCL are pro-
posed. The system is analyzed without DG, implementation 
of DG with FCL and in the absence of FCL. In Manohar 
Singh and Panigrahi (2010) the operating time gap of all 
key relays in the faulted line is minimized. The selectivity 
constrains are added to the existing over current relay con-
straints. To accelerate the convergence, Evolution-based Dif-
ferential Search Algorithm is used to minimize the operating 
time. Intensive researches have been carried out for relay 
coordination issues using several evolutionary-based opti-
mization tools. Particle Swarm Algorithm (PSO) Zeineldin 
et al. (2006), Genetic Algorithm (GA) Singh et al. (S 2012), 
Harmony Search Algorithm (HSA) and Artificial Bee Col-
ony (Uthitsunthorn and Kulworawanichpong  2012) for relay 
coordination have been presented. In Singh et al. (2012) the 
relay selectivity without affecting the sensitivity and fault 
clearing time is achieved for solving coordination of Direc-
tional over current relay. Zellagui et al. (2014) applied Fire-
fly Algorithm (FA) to find the TMS and pick up current 
(Ip) so that the operation time of relay is reduced. Here the 
objective function is single. The inverse definite Minimum 
time directional over current relay is implemented. The relay 
parameters are computed in consideration with the change 
in impedance of the line due to series compensation. The 
relay settings with and without series compensation are com-
pared and discussed. In Hussain et al. (2001) multi-objective 
approach is used to resolve the coordination of DOCRs using 
Modified Firefly Algorithm (MFA). The optimization is per-
formed to yield Time Dial Settings. The pickup currents 
are computed depending on the load current. The research 
reveals that the population size has the impact on the com-
putation time.
In Benabid (2016), the time of operation of all primary 
relay and the operating time of back up relay are the two 
objectives to be minimized simultaneously. The Time Dial 
Settings are taken as real variables and the pickup current 
are taken as integer variables. To balance the real and inte-
ger variables, the enhanced Strength Pareto Evolutionary 
Algorithm 2 is employed. A fuzzy tool is used in addition 
for selecting the best solution. The main challenge in real-
world multi-objective problem is that it is requires high com-
putational simulations. The conventional Multi-Objective 
Evolutionary Algorithms (MOEAs) may take thousands 
of function evaluation which is not practical for real-world 
problems. Hence surrogates are introduced in those MOEAs 
to approximate the fitness evaluations. Classification of 
MOEA with respect to their integration with surrogate mod-
els is presented in Díaz et al. (Javadian and Haghifam 2008). 
Yu et al. (2018) proposed a method where PSO and Social 
learning (SL)-PSO are combined to reach global optimum. 
To increase the optimization efficiency, a surrogate assisted 
PSO is proposed in Cai et al. (2019). The algorithm uses 
global and personal surrogates to update the velocities of 
the particles. The optimization algorithm plays vital role in 
all research areas. Selvi et al. (2020) used genetic algorithm 
for image de-noising process. Senthilselvi et al. (2020) used 
gravitational search algorithm for image restoration process.
The optimal over current relay coordination in power 
distribution system is discussed Chen et al. (2013). The 
type of curve, current setting Tapings and Time dial set-
tings are decided by an experienced engineer to arrive at 
correct settings of relay. More time and cost are needed for 
this procedure. The constraints on the power system are 
reviewed by the engineer for deciding CSM and TSM. The 
constraints may be maximum fault current, the load current, 
fault clearing Time and CT ratios. Since a simple software 
packages do not work with the complex problems, AI tech-
niques such as GA, PSO are implemented to solve the relay 
coordination problem. Setting the relay operating time and 
the relay coordination are complicated as the power system 
encounters various types of loads on different buses, which 
includes static capacitors, large induction motor, power fuses 
and transforms. OCR is connected to the CT, the pickup 
current tuned using CSM and trip time tuned using time 
dial setting multiplier. The overall operating time of all key 
relays is minimized at maximum Fault current. The operat-
ing curves are simulated in accordance with the IEC for the 
required operating time and current range of each DOCR. 
DOCR coordination of a real-time distribution system with 
embedded Renewable Generation is proposed in Kamal et al. 
(2014). The relays fail to operate when there is large out-
age time and huge commercial losses in power plants. The 
operating time of OC relays is set based on an approximate 
equivalent circuit of power grid to estimate the short cir -
cuit currents. A real-time distribution system with Embed-
ded Renewable Generation is taken. Plug setting and Time 
dial setting and type of curve are optimized to give better 
coordination.
Problem formulation
The DOCR relay coordination is a multi-objective problem 
with objectives of relay operating time and coordination 
time. The optimal values of TMS and I p of each relay are 
computed to arrive at better protection coordination.

Surrogate assisted optimization algorithm
In Engineering, many optimization problems are considered 
as global optimization problems. Conventional optimiza -
tion techniques such as Newton method, steepest descent 
are used to solve many engineering optimization problems. 
But they have the limitations, that they are not able to find 
a global solution in case of problems with multiple local 
minima. Hence the conventional optimization algorithms 
are replaced by global optimization algorithms. These algo-
rithms are nowadays used in many engineering problems. 
These algorithms are not knowledge based and provide bet-
ter accurate results. Even though these optimization algo -
rithms are useful to solve complex optimization algorithms, 
they are incapable when the objective function is computa-
tionally complex and expensive, since it requires high num-
ber of iterations and function evaluations. The time taken to 
complete first iteration is somewhat high in these types of 
nature inspired evolutionary algorithms and it is not applied 
to real-world optimization problems with large number of 
function evaluations. Hence nowadays, surrogate assisted 
optimization algorithms are used to solve the computation-
ally expensive real-world optimization problems sub optimi-
zation technique. The surrogate models are used to improve 
the search and converge quickly to the global optimum. The 
surrogate models are built from the random data obtained

Surrogate assisted particle swarm optimization 
algorithm (SAPSO)
Optimization algorithms with great estimating performance 
can solve the complicated real-time problems. Several algo-
rithms such as Genetic Algorithms (GA), Particle Swarm 
Optimization (PSO) algorithm and Differential evolution 
(DE) algorithms are implemented to handle complex real-
world issues. However these algorithms require great num-
ber of fitness evaluations to reach the global optimum solu-
tion which is imposes a great challenge for the real-world 
scenario. The introduction of surrogate models to these 
algorithms reduces the number of fitness evaluations and is 
being implemented practically. The polynomial regression, 
Radial Basis Function Network (RBFN), Artificial Neural 
Network (ANN), Kriging or Gaussian process (GP) and 
Support Vector Machines (SVM) are incorporated as the 
surrogate models (Yu et al. 2018). The SAPSO obtains the 
Pareto optimal solution in case of multi-objective optimiza-
tion technique using less number of fitness evaluations. The 
SAPSO differ from basic PSO in updating mechanism, i.e., 
it is based on surrogates. The number of fitness evaluations 
is reduced by approximating the real-valued function, using 
surrogate models. The surrogate learns a rough contour of 
the fitness landscape in wide search space. RBFN Radial 
Basis Function Network is used as approximation models, 
which is used for function approximation. So in SAPSO the 
convergence is faster compared.

Pseudocode of SAPSO
Step 1:A population of particles is initialised using sam-
pling methods. The particles are assessed by a fitness 
function and the values are updated in exterior files and 
databases.
Step 2: The best value of the particles and the global best 
value of the population of the particles are recorded.
Step 3: An approximate model is constructed using the 
information in the data base. The fitness function is modi-
fied using the approximate model for each objective.
Step 4: Sampling is performed to obtain the solutions and 
are separated as Pareto and non-Pareto solutions.
Step 5: The solutions are updated in exterior files and the 
procedure is repeated until the number of fitness evalua-
tion reaches maximum value (Olivares et al. 2014).
The key feature in SAPSO is the sampling and the clas-
sification of the solutions (Olivares et al. 2014). The param-
eters for SAPSO are shown in Table  1.

Results and discussion
The proposed SAPSO algorithm is evaluated with IEEE 
6 bus and IEEE 30 bus system for both grids connected 
and double configurations. SAPSO based protection 
scheme is explained as flow chart in Fig.  2. All simula-
tions are carried out in MATLAB environment and the 
analysis is performed. In grid connected configuration, 
the system is supplied from grid and DG also. In Double 
configuration, the constraints includes both grid con-
nected and islanded mode, i.e., only DG presents. The 
optimization is carried out first for grid connected mode. 
Then the two modes are considered simultaneously and 
the optimum relay setting is obtained. In this case, the 
relay can satisfactorily work in both modes of operation 
of microgrid.
Case 1: IEEE 6 bus system
The SAPSO is tested with IEEE 6 bus system. It consists 
of 7 lines, 3 generators and 14 relays. Each generator is 
127.5 MW rating. Each line is introduced with midway 
points for indicating where faults are created. Each fault 
position is associated with one primary relay and two or 
three back up relays. The aim of SAPSO is to find the TMS 
and pick up current value by proper settings of relays at 
least computational cost. Three phase faults are created 
in the lines. The algorithm computes the optimal value 
of TMS and pick up current by proper settings of pri -
mary relays. The CT ratios of the relays are presented in 
Table  2.
Grid connected configuration
The values of TMS and pick up current (Ip) are optimized 
and are shown in the Table  3. The relay operating times 
were obtained with best values of TMS, Ip using SAPSO 
algorithm. The value of total TMS of all the relays is com-
puted as 1410 milli seconds and pickup current as1760 milli 
amperes. The TMS values of all the relays R1 to R14 are 
within 0 and 1. Also the pickup current values of all relays 
are optimized according to load currents.
Double configuration
The values of TMS and Ip for grid connected portion of dou-
ble configuration considering both grid connected mode and 
islanded mode simultaneously is shown in Table  4.
The TMS values of all the relays R1–R14 are within 0 and 
1. Also the pickup current IP values of all relays are opti-
mized according to load currents. Table  5 shows the opti -
mal settings for all relays in double configuration. The best 
values of TMS, Ip are computed using SAPSO Algorithm. 
The value of total TMS is computed as 1510 ms and pickup 
current as1920 mA for dual configuration.
As shown in Table  5, the total operating time of all pri-
mary relays is calculated as 9884 ms for single configu-
ration and 12,192 ms for grid connected portion of dual

SAPSO is to find the TMS and pick up current value by

Comparison of multi objective particle swarm 
optimization (MOPSO) With SAPSO
The IEEE 9 bus system is tested with SAPSO and the results 
are compared with MOPSO. From the Table  9, it is inferred 
that the total operating time for MOPSO for single configu-
ration is 14023.2 ms while for SAPSO is 10522 ms.
Similarly for double configuration SAPSO provides low 
operating time of 11,504 ms compared to MOPSO. The 
operating time of R15 under single configuration is 145 ms 
when SAPSO is applied and it is 165 ms when MOPSO is 
applied. Hence SAPSO offers encouraging results in terms 
of operating time. All relays are correctly coordinated. The 
CTI is within the 200 ms and this reveals the optimal coor -
dination between the relays.

the MOPSO in arriving at the solution with same number 
of fitness evaluations.
Conclusion
A SAPSO approach for the optimal coordination of DOCRs 
for both grids connected and double configuration was pre-
sented. Coordination problem is solved using multi-objective 
approach. The CTI was taken as one of the objective along 
the operating time of all relays and investigated consider -
ing grid and autonomous mode constraints simultaneously. 
The protection scheme was tested using standard IEEE 6 
and 30 bus system. For the IEEE 6 bus system the opti-
mal settings of TMS and Ip are computed so that the relay 
employed operates satisfactorily, when micro grid is in grid 
connection mode or it has to perform in islanded mode. The 
total operating time of all primary relays is calculated as 
9884 ms for single configuration and 12,192 ms for grid con-
nected portion of double configuration. Thus the operating
